messages.author: e4a3215063481170
messages.subject: plot without NA of x
parts:
Dear list,

I am trying to plot my data with the x including NA, I understand that I can exclude the NA of x before plotting, however, in the real dataset, this is not an idea choice. I am seeking ways to deal with it in the ggplot code. I have checked out Stack Overflow without any luck. Is there any way I can make the NA group not show in the plot?

A reproducible code looks like below:

set.seed(9992342)
x=c(rep('a',20),rep(NA,20),rep('b',20),rep('c',20),rep('d',20))
y=rnorm(100)
dat=data.frame(x,y)
ggplot(dat,aes(x=as.factor(x),y=y,fill=x))+stat_summary(fun='mean',geom='bar')

Thank you very much.

Best regards,

YA

messages.author: de9071e8091a07a9
messages.subject: Re: plot without NA of x
parts:
Hi,

You can use the pipe operator %>% and dplyr to filter out the NAs from your data without actually excluding them from the data frame. In your example it would be:

dat %>% filter(is.na(x)==F) %>% ggplot(aes(x=as.factor(x),y=y,fill=x))+stat_summary(fun='mean',geom='bar')

Hope that helps.
Lorenzo

messages.subject: Re: plot without NA of x
parts:
Plenty of ways to do that. 
1) you can first save a new data frame without the NAs:

dat2 <- dat[is.na(x) == F, ]

And then plot it:

ggplot(dat2,aes(x=as.factor(x),y=y,fill=x))+stat_summary(fun='mean',geom='bar')

or:

2) you can subset your data within ggplot by doing:

ggplot(dat,aes(x=as.factor(x),y=y,fill=x)) + stat_summary(data = subset(dat, subset = is.na(x) == F), fun='mean',geom='bar')

And I’m sure there are even more.

Best,
Lorenzo

messages.subject: plot grouping info
parts:
Dear Lorenzo and Edjabou, and others,

Thank you very much much. It worked elegantly.

I am now trying to produce a bar chart with two grouping variables, only one of the grouping variables act as the predictor on a continous y. I would like to put info of the two grouping variables within a single bar chart. Could you teach me how to do that please?
A reproducible code looks like below:

ggplot(mtcars,aes(y=mpg,x=as.factor(vs),fill=as.factor(vs),group=as.factor(am)))+stat_summary(fun='mean',geom='bar')

or

ggplot(mtcars,aes(y=mpg,x=as.factor(vs),fill=as.factor(vs)))+stat_summary(fun='mean',geom='bar',aes(group=am))

Both lines produced a bar charts, however, the grouping of am did not work.

Thank you very much.

YA
